spans.text: Busyness is not productivity: beyond about 80% utilization, each extra percent of load buys a disproportionate amount of waiting.
The curve is nearly flat to 70% and then turns into a wall: at 90% an item waits about nine times its service time, at 95% about nineteen.
Utilization is only half the cause;
in arrivals and in the work multiplies the effect, and either alone is survivable.

meaning.text: Kingman's approximation: expected queue time ≈ utilization term × variability term × mean service time.

spans.text: Kingman's formula is an approximation for a single server under heavy load; it overstates the wait at low utilization.
Capacity deliberately left unallocated so that unpredictable work can be absorbed without forming a queue.
Planning to 100% capacity: unplanned work has nowhere to go, so queues are guaranteed.

items.text: Measure utilization per person or team over a few weeks.
Keep 15–20% of capacity unallocated in the plan.
Spend the slack on interruptions first and improvement work second.

spans.text: Waiting depends on utilization and variability together; cut either to shorten queues.
